preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A governance and infrastructure-continuity failure where AI services operating across public, enterprise, sovereign, regulated, government, public-sector, or compliance-bound runtime lanes fail to preserve clear, reliable, auditable separation and controlled permeability between those lanes, causing degraded access, feature fragility, audit-plane impairment, cross-lane opacity, or unclear incident-state reporting. The failure includes feature parity fragility, assurance-wrapper failure, audit-plane degradation, cross-lane incident opacity, governed porosity gaps, sovereign authority non-collapse risk, reverse leakage risk, and authority bleed-through risk. Data leakage, military involvement, or actual compliance breach are risk vectors only unless separately evidenced.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when a sovereign, regulated, public-sector, government, enterprise, or compliance-bound AI runtime lane experiences recurrent or prolonged degradation, feature unavailability, audit/logging impairment, unclear lane-specific status reporting, or dependency opacity showing that the assurance boundary does not reliably preserve service continuity, feature parity, audit-plane continuity, or legible separation from adjacent runtime lanes. The threshold is also met where incident reporting does not make clear which lane, control wrapper, audit plane, feature plane, or shared dependency is degraded, while affected users rely on the lane for compliance-bound work.
